claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fever with suspected or confirmed neutropenia is a medical emergency.** Signs of sepsis = Triage Category 2; at risk of imminent cardiovascular collapse = Category 1; everyone else starts treatment within 30 minutes of arrival (Category 3).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fever** = a single temperature ≥38.5°C, or ≥38.0°C sustained over 1 hour.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Neutropenia** = absolute neutrophil count <500/mm³, or <1000/mm³ with a predicted fall to <500/mm³ over the next 48 hours. **Suspect it** in any oncology patient given oral or IV chemotherapy in the last 14 days, and in other children with recurrent neutropenia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **High-risk cancer treatment protocols:** AML treatment · infant ALL · ALL induction or delayed intensification · lymphoma induction · re-induction for any relapse · allogeneic transplant (day-14 to day+356, as printed) · autologous transplant (day-7 to day +30).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Systemic compromise** = any respiratory support, needing a fluid bolus or inotrope, and/or an altered conscious state.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask to see the Febrile Neutropenia Treatment Card or Letter the patient carries** — it records the diagnosis, risk status and recommended antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Access the CVAD (or a vein) no later than 30 minutes after arrival.** If accessing the CVAD is delayed, insert a peripheral line. ⚠️ **With signs of sepsis, do not wait for anaesthetic cream to work.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods:** FBE and differential, electrolytes and creatinine, 2 sets of blood cultures, group and hold, venous gas and lactate; urine M/C/S. ⚠️ **Do not delay antibiotics waiting for the neutrophil count or the urine.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give the first antibiotic dose by 60 minutes — or by 30 minutes with sepsis/systemic compromise — and make it the broadest, piperacillin-tazobactam.** With a double-lumen CVAD, divide doses down both lumens, or alternate if that is not possible.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stable child:** IV piperacillin-tazobactam 100 mg/kg 6-hourly, max 4 g (the dose is the piperacillin component).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-life-threatening penicillin allergy (rash):** IV cefepime 50 mg/kg 8-hourly, max 2 g (preferred), **or** IV ceftazidime 50 mg/kg 8-hourly, max 2 g.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ceftazidime is weaker against viridans streptococci** — avoid it after recent high-dose methotrexate or cytarabine, with extensive mucositis, or on ciprofloxacin prophylaxis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Life-threatening (immediate) penicillin or beta-lactam allergy:** IV ciprofloxacin 10 mg/kg 12-hourly (max 400 mg) **and** IV vancomycin 15 mg/kg 6-hourly (max 500 mg), aiming for a trough of 10–15 mg/L before the 5th dose.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Add amikacin for systemic compromise/sepsis, high-risk cancer treatment, or FN starting as an inpatient:** 22.5 mg/kg (18 mg/kg if over 10 years) (max 1.5 g) IV 24-hourly, target trough <2 mg/L before the 3rd dose. Regional centres may use another aminoglycoside such as gentamicin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never give an aminoglycoside through the same line at the same time as piperacillin-tazobactam** (or another IV penicillin); flush the line thoroughly with 0.9% sodium chloride before and after each drug.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected resistant Gram-positive infection** (cellulitis, obviously infected line, proven Gram-positive bacteraemia, MRSA colonisation with extensive skin breaks): **add IV vancomycin 15 mg/kg 6-hourly (max 500 mg)**, aiming for a trough of 10–15 mg/L before the 5th dose. **Prolonged fever in a stable child is not an indication for vancomycin.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Abdominal or perineal infection:** add IV/oral metronidazole 7.5 mg/kg 8-hourly (max 500 mg) **only if on cefepime, ceftazidime or ciprofloxacin** — piperacillin-tazobactam already covers anaerobes, except for suspected *C. difficile* colitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Signs of sepsis: 20 mL/kg normal saline IV over no more than 10 minutes (not through a pump).** If improvement is only transient, further boluses up to 40 mL/kg; discuss more than 40 mL/kg with a senior clinician; if no improvement, consider inotropes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Talk every patient through with the on-call oncology fellow/consultant (regional centres: the consultant paediatrician) — after the 1st IV antibiotic dose**, so the call does not delay it.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer to the Primary Treatment Centre** for severe sepsis, deterioration despite broad-spectrum antibiotics, or FN lasting more than 72 hours despite them.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **New CNS symptoms or signs:** CT brain and LP may be indicated — discuss with the on-call oncologist first. ⚠️ **Correct thrombocytopenia and/or coagulopathy before LP.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No routine daily blood cultures in a well, afebrile child.** Repeat one set on Day 2 (± Day 3) only if still febrile.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stop amikacin and/or vancomycin after 24–48 hours** unless the child is clinically unstable or a resistant organism needs them (discuss with Infectious Diseases). **Do not broaden the regimen for persistent fever alone in a stable child.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stop empiric antibiotics with marrow recovery** once blood cultures are negative at 48 hours and the child has been afebrile for at least 24 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Low-risk FN:** consider stopping at 72 hours once blood cultures are negative and the child has had no fever for at least 24 hours — **whatever the marrow recovery** — provided careful follow-up is ensured. Discuss every change, including stopping, with the primary oncology team.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fever beyond 72 hours or recurrent despite broad-spectrum antibiotics: evaluate for invasive fungal infection.** Empiric antifungal: **amphotericin** (caspofungin or voriconazole if contraindicated). IFI high risk — start it; IFI low risk — consider it.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **High risk for IFI:** relapsed acute leukaemia · AML · GvHD · allogeneic HSCT · severe aplastic anaemia · prolonged corticosteroids · prolonged ICU stay.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever and suspected or confirmed neutropenia' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_suspected_or_confirmed_neutropenia/, retrieved 2026-09-23
